title: Origin Check Register
one_liner: Inventories every AI model a regulated small firm uses, including inside vendors, and flags where each one comes from.
speaker: Salim Ismail and Dave Blundin
context: Salim predicts a hard push against Chinese open-source models after a study found auto-generated backdoors. Dave expects banking, insurance and other regulated industries to bar them entirely, and research labs to follow.
customer: US community banks, credit unions, independent insurance agencies, fintech startups and small federal contractors with 20–500 staff
problem: These firms often don't know which AI models are running in their tools. Many SaaS vendors quietly embed open-weight models. When an examiner, a prime contractor or a client asks them to prove no restricted-origin models are in use, they have no answer and no register.
revenue_model: Fixed-fee inventory and register, about $2,500–$6,000 per firm, then about $300 a month to keep it current as vendors change (estimate)
why_now: The hosts expect an imminent policy push against Chinese models in regulated and government-adjacent work, triggered by the espionage story and backdoor research. Firms that get ahead of it can answer vendor questionnaires before rules land.
first_steps: Write a one-page 'AI model origin questionnaire' to send to software vendors and test it on 5 common SaaS tools
Offer a free 30-minute model inventory call to 10 credit unions or insurance agencies on LinkedIn
Build the register template plus a sample report from one real (anonymised) inventory and quote a fixed price
cost_to_start: About 1–2 weeks and under $300 for a site, templates and outreach tooling
competition: Broad AI-governance platforms and GRC consultancies exist, but most are pricey and not focused on model provenance for small regulated firms
risks: The predicted restrictions may never become formal rules. Vendors may refuse to disclose which models they use. Big GRC platforms may add a provenance field. It must not drift into legal advice, so frame it as an inventory, not a compliance opinion.

tool.title: Model Origin Sorter
tool.one_liner: Paste the AI tools and models your firm uses and get an origin-flagged register you can hand to an auditor.
tool.demo: The customer pastes a list of tools, models or API names, one per line, with an optional vendor column. The page matches each entry against a bundled table of common model families and lists their developer, developer country, licence type and whether the weights are open. Anything it can't match goes into a 'needs vendor answer' list, with a pre-written email to send the vendor. Output is a downloadable CSV register and a printable summary.
tool.data_plan: The customer's own list, plus a bundled, hand-curated table of well-known model families (developer, country, licence) from public model cards, with a 'last checked' date. No episode figures are used.
acceptance: Pasting a list that includes 'Llama 3', 'Qwen2.5' and 'MyVendorBot' shows three rows: two matched with developer and country, and 'MyVendorBot' under 'Needs vendor answer'
Clicking 'Example' loads a 10-item sample list and fills the register and summary without typing
'Download CSV' produces a file whose rows match the on-screen register
Each unmatched item has a 'Copy vendor email' button that copies a questionnaire mentioning that tool's name
The page shows a visible note that the table is curated reference data with a last-checked date, not legal advice
